items.title: Harry Potter: Visions of Magic
items.description: Three large-scale immersive attractions brought the wizarding world to life across four continents — a permanent installation in Singapore and two traveling units touring Europe and the Americas. I managed the media and interactive technology production of a high-stakes multi-market touring operation, overseeing vendor contracts, client and partner relationships, and on-site coordination across all three instances. Holding the creative integrity of beloved IP at global scale was the defining challenge.

media.caption: Led the design and production of an immersive touring journey that brings the wizarding world to life through artful, interactive environments.
A bespoke interactive wand gives visitors agency, triggering hidden effects and revealing layers of the story.
The environments remix iconic IP into a contemporary multi-sensory experience for global audiences.

items.title: Manhunt
items.description: The title sequence for Apple TV+'s Manhunt had to make 160-year-old imagery feel urgent — dropping viewers into the 12-day hunt for Lincoln's assassin before a single scene played. I led pre through post: sourcing and licensing media from the Lincolnian Archives at the Library of Congress, then overseeing colorization, projection mapping, 3D visualization, live action, and animation. The result functions as both historical artifact and psychological pressure.

media.caption: Our title sequence drops viewers into the 12-day chase for Lincoln's killer.
The sequence uses restored, colorized, and projection-mapped Civil War imagery with live action and animation.
A corrosive visual treatment evokes damaged 1800s photographic processes and rising national tension.
Kinetic editorial pacing, photogrammetry, and original music build the pressure of a historical thriller.

items.title: Before
items.description: The title sequence for Apple TV+'s Before locates grief as atmosphere — something that never fully lifts rather than an event that passes. Shot on infrared cameras with vintage lenses, it builds a dreamscape where emotional memory bleeds into the present. I oversaw post-production, guiding editorial and visual development with sustained restraint — every choice in service of feeling.

media.caption: Digital Kitchen shaped an unsettling title sequence for Before around grief, loss, and ties to the past.
The visual approach blends archival and modern looks into a dreamscape where time feels directionless.
Infrared digital cameras and vintage lenses helped create the sequence's otherworldly atmosphere.

items.title: Pocket Garden
items.description: At Google I/O, Pocket Garden made GPS-based VPS technology legible to developers for the first time — turning abstract geospatial API capability into a living AR experience anchored to real-world coordinates. I steered production at BUCK, managing creative and technical delivery of a demo that had to work flawlessly on a global stage. The project required making infrastructure feel like magic without obscuring what it could actually do.

media.caption: Pocket Garden showcased Google's Geospatial API through an open source AR demo for developers.
The experience turned real-world location data into a playful spatial garden for Google I/O.
BUCK's demo used ARCore and location-aware interaction to explore how digital objects can inhabit public space.
The project paired developer utility with a friendly visual system designed to make VPS technology legible.

items.title: Faith and Liberty Discovery Center
items.description: The Faith and Liberty Discovery Center set out to reframe the American Bible Society's legacy through civic values — Liberty, Justice, and Hope — powered by rich interactive and tangible media. As Interactive and Creative Technology lead at Local Projects, I oversaw content development, interactive exhibitry, RFP and ROM for a bespoke tangible media device system, and coordination across a complex multidisciplinary partner network. I held the production through the content development and design phase.

media.caption: Local Projects designed the museum as an immersive exploration of values behind American democracy.
The visit centers on Liberty, Justice, and Hope through media-rich galleries instead of a traditional timeline.
Visitors use a digital torch called The Lamp to collect resonant quotes, songs, and stories.
The Unity gallery weaves individual choices into a collective data portrait.

items.title: New York City Ballet Art Series
items.description: Santtu Mustonen's handcrafted visual universe became an immersive multimedia installation in the Promenade of Lincoln Center's David H. Koch Theater, setting the tone for an entire NYCB season. I produced the installation end to end — navigating the logistical and curatorial demands of one of New York's most prestigious venues while preserving the integrity of the artist's singular vision. The work demanded fluency across fine art, performance, and spatial design simultaneously.

media.caption: Combining handcrafted imagery with new technologies, Santtu Mustonnen presents an exhilirating immersive experience for New York City Ballet's 2017 Art Series.

items.title: Spotify Year in Music
items.description: Before Wrapped was Wrapped, there was Year in Music — the inaugural Spotify campaign that made listening data feel personal for the first time. I led production of the WebGL experience and API integration at Stink Studios, delivering a platform across 35 languages and 57 countries. We established the creative and technical blueprint for what became one of the most celebrated annual digital experiences in the world.

media.caption: Stink Studios partnered with Spotify to turn listener data into personalized Year in Music insights.
The WebGL centerpiece used Spotify's API, custom shaders, gradients, and duotone effects to visualize the year.
A custom CMS supported copy updates and translations across 35 languages and 57 countries.

items.title: Robert Rauschenberg Foundation
items.description: Rauschenberg made work that refused categorization — his foundation's digital home needed to match that restlessness. I led design, development, and launch of the Foundation portal in Drupal, building a living archive of his artwork, writing, programs, and legacy in a system designed to grow. The challenge was creating infrastructure that felt as dynamic as his practice without imposing a curatorial voice that didn't belong there.

media.caption: The Robert Rauschenberg Foundation site brings together the artist's work, archives, programs, and legacy.

items.title: DreamboxXx
items.description: DreamboxXx was a love letter to underground community — a custom arcade cabinet housing nine original games, built for the Dreamhouse Queens, a queer safe space and DIY tech collective in Brooklyn. I produced the full project: cabinet fabrication, game development pipeline, residency programming, and the grand opening and closing celebrations. It wasn't a commission — it was a community gift, which meant the standard was set by the people it was made for.

media.caption: The custom cabinet features nine games by queer designers built around an unusual shared-button control scheme.
The residency paired Dreamhouse's community space with DBAA's collaborative arcade-building practice.

items.title: Sally LaPointe
items.description: Sally LaPointe's aesthetic — minimal, precise, quietly radical — demanded a digital presence that matched her eye without getting in its way. I led creative direction, design, development, launch, and ongoing management, building a Magento e-commerce platform with a streamlined UI and fluid page-to-page animation. The site became the hub for her ready-to-wear collections and brand collaborations, holding the brand standard across every touchpoint.

items.title: Armand de Brignac
items.description: Jay-Z's champagne lives at the intersection of luxury, culture, and aspiration — and its digital presence had to hold that position without blinking. I led a multi-year integrated partnership covering web design and development, content production, and social strategy from concept through execution. Over the engagement I built the systems, visual language, and content cadence that gave Armand de Brignac a digital identity worthy of the bottle.
